content: The image shows soybean stems with small black specks throughout the tissue, giving a marbled/charcoal-sprinkled appearance. This is strongly suggestive of Charcoal Rot. Let me compare with reference images.

The test image shows mature, dead soybean stems with small black specks on the outer surface in a somewhat linear pattern on bleached stems. This matches Diaporthe (pod and stem blight) - characterized by "black, raised specks (pycnidia) appearing in linear rows on mature soybean stems." The Diaporthe reference (bottom-right panel) shows a very similar pattern. The black specks are on the external stem surface, distinguishing from Charcoal Rot where microsclerotia are beneath the epidermis internally.
